v1.feedback: The gravity-reversal-as-deus-ex-machina is a genuinely clever read of the brief and the warm→cool color swerve lands, but the form is a single subdividing catenary that will read thin and sparse for most of its 22-second cycle — consider spawning 4-6 parallel string curves at different depths and x-offsets (closer to actual Gonzalez-Torres curtains) so the lift moment has more mass to dramatize. The z-axis noise is too low (0.002) to give the cloud real depth, making it essentially a flat ribbon in 3D; bump per-vertex z-scatter during subdivision to ±0.3 so orbit reveals volume. Finally, the swerve moment itself could hit harder if you briefly spike point size and bloom intensity at LIFT_PEAK rather than only shifting hue — right now the color shift alone may be too subtle at a glance.

v2.feedback: The Gonzalez-Torres light-curtain concept is legible and the cyclic gravity-reversal 'deus ex machina' lift is a genuine swerve, but the timing is too slow — 14s before anything happens means most viewers see only drooping strings. The palette shift during lift (warm → cool white) is tasteful but subtle to the point of invisibility; push the hue separation harder so the divine moment reads in 2s. The five strings feel sparse for a curtain; doubling count and tightening spacing would give the bead-curtain density that makes Gonzalez-Torres' work iconic. Consider shortening the cycle to ~24s and making the lift apex more dramatic (strings fully taut/horizontal) so the swerve actually surprises rather than gently sighing.
